paper_metadata.title: Towards Pricing Financial Derivatives with an IBM Quantum Computer

summary: The paper reports qPCA-style estimation of dominant eigenvectors/eigenvalues for 2×2, 3×3, and 4×4 interest-rate covariance matrices on IBMQX2, using 3 qubits for the 2×2 case, 5 qubits for the 3×3 case, and 3 qubits for the 4×4 case. The 2×2 experiment converged in 4 iterations with an estimated largest eigenvalue of 0.8576 and simulator fidelity 0.977 for the eigenvector stage; the 4×4 hardware run was too noisy to be useful, with estimated coefficient error over 100%.

experiments.description: qPCA-based estimation of the dominant eigenvector/eigenvalue for a 2×2 interest-rate forward-rate cross-correlation matrix using a 5-qubit IBM superconducting device and Qiskit, with iterative eigenvector refinement and quantum phase estimation.

algorithm.variant: quantum principal component analysis (qPCA) with iterative eigenvector refinement and QPE
algorithm.convergence_criteria: iterate until estimated eigenvector coefficients stabilize; paper reports stopping after 4 iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 2×2 covariance matrix normalized by trace and encoded into a 1-qubit eigenvector register with 2 ancilla qubits for 2-bit eigenvalue estimation
problem_formulation.objective_function: estimate the dominant eigenvector/eigenvalue of the normalized covariance matrix rho2 via qPCA
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: post-selection on the measured eigenvalue subspace |11>

problem_instance.description: 2×2 submatrix of the 3×3 forward-rate cross-correlation matrix based on historical interest-rate data for two time-maturing forward rates
problem_instance.dataset_name: historical forward-rate cross-correlation data (from Wilmott textbook figure)

dataset_specification.description: 2×2 submatrix extracted from the 3×3 covariance matrix in Eq. (12); maturities correspond to two forward rates

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: normalize covariance matrix by its trace to form rho2
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 4 iterative runs, each averaged over 8192 realizations; compare estimated coefficients across iterations and across measurement bases

noise_model.error_mitigation_method: measurement in x, y, and arbitrary bases with averaging to reduce systematic errors

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: normalize covariance matrix by trace; compute target eigen-decomposition classically for comparison
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: extract eigenvector coefficients from measurement statistics; compare to exact eigenvector

speedup_claims.conditions: small 2x2 matrix; paper does not claim a concrete speedup for this experiment
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper frames this as a proof-of-principle qPCA/QPE experiment on IBMQX2, not as a speedup demonstration.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not established; only a 2×2 toy matrix on a 5-qubit device.
limiting_factors: Hardware noise and limited qubit count

notes: The paper explicitly states use of the 5-qubit IBMQX2 processor and 3 qubits for the 2×2 case (2 ancilla + 1 eigenvector qubit). No circuit depth or gate counts are reported for this experiment. The paper discusses qPCA/QPE conceptually but does not provide asymptotic complexity for this specific experiment.
The paper presents a proof-of-principle qPCA/QPE experiment and does not claim a demonstrated quantum advantage over classical methods.
